cookies.description: Cookie Policy of the Auxilium platform
cookies.title: Cookie Policy

section1.title: 1. Definitions
section1.content: For the purposes of this Cookie Policy, the following definitions apply: Cookies — small text files stored on the User's end device by the web browser, containing data required for the proper functioning of the website; Service — the Auxilium platform available at auxilium.app; End Device — a computer, phone, tablet or other device through which the User accesses the Service; Session — the period of User activity on the Service from login to logout or browser closure; Controller — KPZ's Productions, the entity responsible for processing data within the Service.

section2.title: 2. Types of cookies used
section2.content: The Auxilium Service uses the following types of cookies by storage duration: session cookies — deleted automatically when the browser session ends; persistent cookies — stored on the User's device for a specified period or until manually deleted. By purpose: necessary cookies — required for the correct operation of the Service and cannot be disabled; functional cookies — remembering User preferences, such as interface language; analytical cookies — collecting anonymous statistical data about Service usage; marketing cookies — used for potential content personalisation.

section3.title: 3. Cookies necessary for the operation of the service
section3.content: Necessary cookies are required for the correct operation of the platform and cannot be disabled without losing core functionality. They include: session authentication tokens ensuring secure login; active workspace identifier (active_space_id); JWT session token stored in an httpOnly cookie with a 24-hour expiry; interface language settings. The legal basis for processing data through necessary cookies is the necessity to perform the electronic services agreement (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) and the Controller's legitimate interest in ensuring platform security (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

section4.title: 4. Analytical and statistical cookies
section4.content: Analytical cookies allow us to collect anonymous information about how the Service is used, including: number of visits, time spent on the page, pages viewed by Users, and traffic sources. This data is used exclusively to improve platform functionality and content and is not linked to data identifying individual Users. Analytical cookies are installed only after obtaining the User's voluntary consent, which may be withdrawn at any time without affecting the lawfulness of processing carried out before withdrawal.

section5.title: 5. Marketing and personalisation cookies
section5.content: Marketing cookies may be used to personalise content based on User behaviour on the Service. Currently, the Auxilium Service does not use third-party marketing cookies for advertising purposes. Should such cookies be introduced, Users will be informed in advance and asked to provide separate, informed consent in accordance with the requirements of the ePrivacy Directive (2002/58/EC) and GDPR. Any marketing cookies will be clearly described in the updated version of this policy.

section6.title: 6. Managing cookie settings
section6.content: Users can manage cookies through: web browser settings — it is possible to block or restrict cookie storage or delete cookies already stored; the consent management panel available upon first visit to the Service. Disabling necessary cookies may prevent login and use of the platform. Cookie management instructions for popular browsers: Chrome — chrome://settings/cookies; Firefox — about:preferences#privacy; Safari — Preferences > Privacy; Microsoft Edge — edge://settings/cookies.

section7.title: 7. Cookie consent and its withdrawal
section7.content: Upon first visiting the Service, Users are informed about the cookies in use and asked to give voluntary consent to optional cookies (analytical, marketing) in accordance with Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR. Consent may be withdrawn at any time without giving reasons and without negative consequences for the User — withdrawal of consent for analytical or marketing cookies does not restrict access to core platform features. Consent may be withdrawn by changing cookie settings in the browser or in the Service's consent management panel.

section8.title: 8. Changes to the cookie policy
section8.content: The Controller reserves the right to update this Cookie Policy as technology, law, or Service functionality changes. All changes will be published at auxilium.app/cookies together with the effective date. Users will be notified of significant changes via a message displayed in the Service or electronically. For questions regarding cookies, please contact: kontakt@auxilium.app.

privacy.description: Privacy Policy and Personal Data Protection of the Auxilium platform
privacy.title: Privacy Policy

section1.title: 1. Data Controller
section1.content: The controller of personal data of users of the Auxilium platform is KPZ's Productions (hereinafter: 'Controller'). For matters concerning personal data protection, you may contact the Controller at: kontakt@auxilium.app. The Controller processes personal data in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016 (GDPR), the Polish Act of 10 May 2018 on the Protection of Personal Data, and other applicable legislation.

section2.title: 2. Scope of personal data collected
section2.content: The Controller collects the following categories of personal data: identification data (name, username); contact data (email address); service usage data (subscription plans, payment history); technical data (IP address, browser type, session identifiers); data entered by the User while using the platform (projects, leads, client and employee data). Provision of mandatory data is a condition for using the platform. Provision of other data is voluntary.

section3.title: 3. Purposes and legal bases for processing
section3.content: Personal data are processed for the following purposes and on the following legal bases: performance of contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) — account registration, platform service delivery, payment processing; compliance with legal obligations (Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR) — issuing VAT invoices, retaining accounting records for the required period; legitimate interest of the Controller (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR) — platform security, direct marketing to existing customers, pursuit of potential claims; consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR) — marketing communications to new users, optional cookies.

section4.title: 4. Recipients of personal data
section4.content: Personal data may be shared with the following categories of recipients: payment processors (Stripe Inc.) to the extent necessary for subscription payment processing; cloud infrastructure and hosting providers (Vercel Inc., Supabase Inc., Upstash Inc.) to the extent necessary for platform service delivery; email service providers used for communication with Users; public authorities entitled to receive data under applicable law. The Controller does not sell Users' personal data to third parties for commercial purposes.

section5.title: 5. Data retention period
section5.content: Personal data are retained for the duration of the contract, and thereafter: for 5 years — data required for tax and accounting purposes; for 3 years from contract termination — data required for potential civil claims; until consent is withdrawn or the purpose is achieved — data processed on the basis of consent. Upon expiry of the retention period, data are permanently deleted or anonymised in a manner preventing attribution to a specific person.

section6.title: 6. Rights of data subjects
section6.content: Every User has the right to: access their personal data and obtain a copy (Art. 15 GDPR); rectification of inaccurate or incomplete data (Art. 16 GDPR); erasure of data in cases specified in Art. 17 GDPR (right to be forgotten); restriction of processing (Art. 18 GDPR); data portability in a machine-readable format (Art. 20 GDPR); object to processing based on legitimate interest (Art. 21 GDPR); withdraw consent at any time without negative consequences. Requests may be submitted to: kontakt@auxilium.app. The Controller will respond without undue delay and within one month. Users have the right to lodge a complaint with the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (UODO), ul. Stawki 2, 00-193 Warsaw, Poland.

section7.title: 7. Transfer of data outside the European Economic Area
section7.content: Some recipients of data, in particular Stripe Inc. and Vercel Inc., are based in the United States. Transfers of data to these entities are based on standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission (Art. 46(2)(c) GDPR), which ensure an adequate level of personal data protection. Users may obtain a copy of the applicable clauses by contacting the Controller at kontakt@auxilium.app.

section8.title: 8. Data security
section8.content: The Controller applies appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure the security of personal data, including: data transmission encryption using the TLS/HTTPS protocol; storage of passwords exclusively in encrypted form using the Argon2 algorithm; access controls restricting data access to authorised personnel and processors only; regular data backups. In the event of a personal data breach, the Controller will notify the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours, and Users without undue delay if the breach is likely to result in a high risk to their rights and freedoms.

section9.title: 9. Contact for data protection matters
section9.content: For matters related to personal data processing, please contact us: by email at kontakt@auxilium.app; in writing to the registered address of KPZ's Productions. The Controller will respond without undue delay and within one month of receiving the request. In justified, complex cases, this period may be extended by a further 2 months, and the Controller will promptly inform the applicant in writing of the reasons for the delay.

section10.title: 10. Changes to the privacy policy
section10.content: The Controller reserves the right to make changes to this privacy policy in connection with legal, technological, or organisational changes. All changes will be published at auxilium.app/privacy and will take effect on the date indicated with each change, no earlier than 14 days after publication. Users will be notified of significant changes by email to the address provided at registration. Continued use of the platform after the changes take effect constitutes acceptance.
